appraisal_events.evidence: Swann qui avait pris dans le milieu Guermantes l'habitude de recevoir les grands artistes comme de bons amis à qui on cherche seulement à faire manger les plats qu'ils aiment, jouer aux jeux ou... se livrer aux sports qui leur plaisent.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator glosses Swann's flattering remark as habitual social behavior learned from the Guermantes set, reducing his treatment of great artists to indulging their tastes rather than engaging their minds, a mildly deflating characterization of Swann.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Il a dit à maman qu'il vous avait trouvé extrêmement intelligent. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte reports that Bergotte praised the narrator as extremely intelligent, directly countering the narrator's own fear that he had seemed stupid, staging him as favorably regarded by the admired writer.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's compliment is framed by the narrator as a social habit of superficially indulging artists rather than genuine intellectual engagement, a mild deflation of his sincerity.
Being reported as found 'extremely intelligent' by Bergotte elevates the narrator's standing as a credible interlocutor, reversing his own anxious self-doubt.

ambiguities: Swann's flattering remark to the narrator is filtered through the narrator's own ironic gloss on Swann's social habits, so the negative coloring attaches more to Swann's manner of hosting artists than to the sincerity of the specific compliment.

Bergotte's praise of the narrator reaches the reader only secondhand, via Gilberte's report of what he told 'maman', so its narrative reliability rests on Gilberte's account rather than direct witness.
